body: [{"streamId":"01a0c941-fb35-7536-9f5b-0b473c0ab22a","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Decision.DecisionRecorded","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a0c941-fb35-7536-9f5b-0b473c0ab22a\u0022,\u0022Scope\u0022:\u0022Project\u0022,\u0022ScopeId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71\u0022,\u0022Statement\u0022:\u0022**A pull request the daemon opens reads like the owner wrote it for a colleague: the platform\\u0027s \\u0060pr-summary\\u0060 skill asks for a body sized to the diff, in the owner\\u0027s own voice, with no standing sections, and the daemon adds nothing around that prose but the work-item link.** Why: bioage-calculator pull request #4 (ARX-5817, task 4442dd3a, run 01a0b659-20e8) opened on 2026-09-18 with a 3,837-byte, 36-line body for a 56-line added file, and the session had followed the installed skill exactly. The wall was what the skill asked for: no sizing rule anywhere in it, and a standing \\u0060## For the reviewer\\u0060 section the skill itself called \\u0022often the most valuable part\\u0022, which on a change with nothing to flag got filled with a repeat of the run handoff. About 70 percent of that body was the agent\\u0027s prose and the rest was the platform\\u0027s own additions. arx-platform #2117 and #2121 were rewritten by hand on 2026-09-17 for the same reasons (idea efdea16d). Ruled by Brian in the hall9k project window on 2026-09-19. **The skill is rebuilt on arx-platform\\u0027s own rule.** \\u0060.claude/skills/pr-summary/SKILL.md\\u0060 is rewritten with \\u0060.claude/commands/git/pr-description.md\\u0060 from arx-platform as its base, which Brian judged about 90 percent reusable generically: read the change rather than the commit subjects, how it should read, the keep-out list, the bad-then-good example pair, and the title rule all carry over, while the ARX key form and that repository\\u0027s own standards document are generalized or labelled as one repository\\u0027s example. The standing \\u0060## For the reviewer\\u0060 heading is gone: what a reviewer must do or watch for appears inline, only when it exists, and the run handoff never appears in the body at all. A sizing rule is stated outright (the body is proportionate to the diff; a one-file or documentation-only change gets one or two sentences of orientation plus only the judgment calls and reviewer actions that actually exist) and a worked small-change body sits beside the large one, so \\u0022three or four lines is a finished body\\u0022 is shown rather than asserted. A repository that ships its own PR-description rule still wins for the prose, exactly as before. **The voice is the owner\\u0027s, found rather than only named.** The skill and \\u0060WorkPromptBuilder.AppendPullRequestSummaryStep\\u0060 both say: load the voice skill \\u0060h9k owner set --voice-skill\\u0060 named (#193, unchanged and not rebuilt here), and failing that look for one called \\u0060my-voice\\u0060 in the owner\\u0027s own user skills directory and then in the repository\\u0027s \\u0060.claude/skills/\\u0060, load it with its code-review context, and write in it; when neither tier has one, say so and use the rule\\u0027s own plain colleague voice. The repository\\u0027s PR-description rule keeps the structure either way. The fallback is deliberately local to this one step rather than folded into \\u0060AppendOwnerVoiceRule\\u0060, which every other voiced seam shares: a pull request body is the artifact this ruling is about, and widening the search everywhere would have moved seams this ruling never looked at. **The prompt step says the three things the skill cannot.** It names the sizing rule; it names what to leave out, which is now the work-item link the platform writes, a restatement of the diff, build and test attestations, whatever the same message is already carrying under \\u0060HANDOFF:\\u0060, and any restatement of the acceptance criteria; and it tells the session to write the external key in the same form the repository\\u0027s own commit subjects use, with a colon where they use one and without where they do not, rather than the \\u0060KEY: title\\u0060 shape \\u0060PullRequestBody.WithExternalKey\\u0060 has to choose when it repairs a title carrying no key at all. Both recompose protocols get it, and prompt-builder tests cover the voiced and the unvoiced rendering. **The daemon\\u0027s own additions are deleted**, which is #163\\u0027s amendment above rather than a second decision: the body is the work-item line, rendered as \\u0060[\\u003Ckey\\u003E](\\u003Curl\\u003E)\\u0060, and the session\\u0027s prose, and nothing else. *Rejected: a setting to keep the additions*, for the reason recorded there. **Does this block the later vision?** No. This is prose in a skill, prose in one prompt step, and a deletion inside one pure composer; this node already holding it says so; another node holding it queues a \\u0060MessageKind.ClaimRequest\\u0060 envelope (\\u0060ClaimEnvelopeCodec.ClaimRequestRecord\\u0060: task, requester node/owner/fingerprint, reason, and \\u2014 for a gated project \\u2014 this install\\u0027s own tracker identity, read locally via the new \\u0060TrackerAssignmentTake.ResolveOwnIdentityAsync\\u0060 since the granting node has no other way to learn it) addressed to the holder\\u0027s own node, and prints that it asked and is waiting. Queued only, the \\u0060h9k message send\\u0060 convention \\u2014 this command never touches the transport itself; the daemon\\u0027s own message sweep sends it. **The answer.** A new hosted service, \\u0060ClaimRequestWatchLoop\\u0060, polls this node\\u0027s own received-but-unhandled messages of all three \\u0060MessageKind.MechanicalKindValues\\u0060 kinds on the ordinary sweep cadence: a \\u0060ClaimRequest\\u0060 is handed to the new \\u0060Hall9k.Connectors.WorkItems.ClaimRequestEngine.ReceiveRequestAsync\\u0060, and a \\u0060ClaimGranted\\u0060/\\u0060ClaimRefused\\u0060 reply is only decoded far enough to log a malformed body and marked handled \\u2014 the requester\\u0027s own answer already arrives through the replicated \\u0060TaskHolderReleased\\u0060/\\u0060TaskTakeRefused\\u0060 event \\u0060h9k task show\\u0060/\\u0060h9k status\\u0060 actually read, so the reply itself carries nothing this node does not already have (fix, independent pre-PR review, cycle 1, adversarial lens: before this, nothing on the receiving node ever read or handled either reply kind, so it sat received-and-unhandled forever) \\u2014 the one engine both the automatic reaction and \\u0060h9k task grant\\u0060/\\u0060refuse\\u0060 reach, so \\u0022grant runs the auto release\\u0022 is literally the same method call. It always appends \\u0060TaskTakeRequested\\u0060 first (parking the ask on the task\\u0027s own stream, so \\u0060h9k task show\\u0060/\\u0060h9k status\\u0060 can name who asked and why even before anything is decided), then reads the project\\u0027s own \\u0060take-policy\\u0060 (new setting, \\u0060TakePolicy\\u0060 value object, \\u0060Auto\\u0060/\\u0060Ask\\u0060, default \\u0060Auto\\u0060, \\u0060NodeScoped\\u0060\\u002B\\u0060ProjectScoped\\u0060 like \\u0060ClaimGate\\u0060): \\u0060Ask\\u0060 stops there, parked for the holder\\u0027s own human; \\u0060Auto\\u0060 checks for a live run on this node for the task (\\u0060ClaimRequestEngine.FindLiveRunAsync\\u0060, the identical four live \\u0060RunState\\u0060s \\u0060RunSupervisor.StopRunsSupersededByTakeoverAsync\\u0060 already reads) and either grants or refuses immediately. **The grant.** \\u0060ClaimRequestEngine.GrantAsync\\u0060 (also \\u0060h9k task grant \\u003Cid\\u003E\\u0060\\u0027s own body): \\u0060TaskLedgerHolder.TryReleaseAsync\\u0060 releases the ledger holder by conditional write through A1 \\u2014 an ordinary release, not an override, since this is the current holder giving the task up cooperatively rather than being overridden \\u2014 then \\u0060TaskDecider.GrantTake\\u0060 appends \\u0060TaskHolderReleased\\u0060 extended with \\u0060GrantedToNodeId\\u0060/\\u0060GrantedToOwnerId\\u0060 (both null, and both this call\\u0027s own new optional fields, for every ordinary release before and after this feature), whose \\u0060Apply\\u0060 reassigns \\u0060AssignedOwnerId\\u0060 to the requester and lands the task back on Queued/Blocked exactly the shape \\u0060TaskHolderTakenOver\\u0060 already gives a forced takeover \\u2014 so the requester\\u0027s own node (or a sibling node under the same owner, racing its own \\u0060TryClaimAsync\\u0060) claims it through the ordinary dispatch sweep, no bespoke claim mechanism of its own. A gated project\\u0027s tracker assignee moves to the requester\\u0027s own account best effort, through a new \\u0060TrackerAssignmentTake.GrantToAsync\\u0060 (writes an explicit identity rather than resolving this install\\u0027s own, the one thing \\u0060TakeAsync\\u0060 cannot do since a grant\\u0027s whole point is putting somebody ELSE\\u0027s identity on the item) \\u2014 a failure there (no tracker identity carried, or the write could not be confirmed) never blocks or reverses the grant, only names the hand step in a warning. A \\u0060MessageKind.ClaimGranted\\u0060 envelope is queued for the requester. **The refusal.** \\u0060ClaimRequestEngine.RefuseAsync\\u0060 (also \\u0060h9k task refuse \\u003Cid\\u003E --reason\\u0060\\u0027s own body) appends \\u0060TaskTakeRefused\\u0060 naming the requester and the reason (a live run\\u0027s own start time for an automatic refusal) and queues push\\u0022 and returned without ever calling the renumberer, true for the rebase itself but never true for a placeholder nothing else on the mechanical paths ever assigns a number to (task 609bd344 run 01a0b500, PR #479: two fetch failures an hour apart with no renumbering line either time, then the same run\\u0027s dirty-worktree skip with its PR opened five seconds later). **The fix.** A new \\u0060TryRenumberDecisionsLogPlaceholderOnSkipAsync\\u0060 runs at every one of those skip sites, both inside \\u0060EnsureRebasedBeforeFinalPassAsync\\u0060\\u0027s own try block and wrapped around its call into the shared \\u0060RebasePreflightAsync\\u0060 \\u2014 never from \\u0060RebaseOntoStackedParentAsync\\u0060\\u0027s own call into that same preflight, so a stacked child\\u0027s own placeholder stays exactly as unrenumbered as Decisions Log #162 already scopes it. It reads this branch\\u0027s own locally known \\u0060origin/\\u003Cbase\\u003E\\u0060, confirms the worktree is genuinely still checked out on this run\\u0027s own branch first (self-review finding: a wrong-branch skip must never compute a merge base, let alone a commit, against whatever HEAD happens to name), rejects a worktree with any staged or uncommitted change to a tracked file (the citation sweep can force-stage and commit any tracked file it rewrites, not only PLAN.md), and \\u2014 only when that local ref already equals this branch\\u0027s own merge base, the identical no-op shape the existing renumbering call already trusts \\u2014 runs \\u0060DecisionsLogRenumberer.RenumberIfNeededAsync\\u0060 and records \\u0060RunRebasedOntoBase\\u0060 with \\u0060WasNoOp: true\\u0060 exactly as the pre-existing no-op path does, raising the same mandatory gate over the moved tip. Origin having moved further than the locally known ref confirms is left alone rather than committed against a base this branch was never actually rebased onto. A caller that cannot vouch the locally known ref is fresh \\u2014 its own fetch just failed, an exception could have interrupted one in flight, or the preflight refused before any fetch was attempted at all \\u2014 routes through a new \\u0060RefetchAndTryRenumberDecisionsLogPlaceholderOnSkipAsync\\u0060 first, which retries the fetch once under whatever repository lock the caller already holds and leaves the placeholder for a later pass if that retry also fails, rather than judging the no-op test against a ref of unknown age and risking a number some other branch already claimed on the base\\u0027s real, current tip; the one retargeted-base refusal skips this retry entirely; that refusal means \\u0060baseBranch\\u0060 is not even the pull request\\u0027s real base anymore, so no fetch of it is ever this branch\\u0027s own to judge freshness against. **The closeout guard.** A new, read-only \\u0060DecisionsLogRenumberer.TailEntryIsThisTasksUnresolvedPlaceholderAsync\\u0060 lets \\u0060CloseoutEngine.TryAutoMergeAsync\\u0060 check PLAN.md\\u0027s own tail immediately before its merge call: every stacked shape that would still owe a replay lap to renumber it (the existing \\u0060ParentMergedAligned\\u0060 \\u0060StackReplay\\u0060 dispatch) has already had its chance earlier the same sweep, so a placeholder surviving to this check parks instead of merging an unnumbered entry onto the project\\u0027s base. **Tests.** Three \\u0060ReviewEngineTests\\u0060 exercise the skip paths against a real git worktree and origin: a permanently broken origin remote leaves the placeholder for a later pass rather than risk a duplicate number against a base the run could no longer confirm was current; an untracked file left dirty in the worktree still gets the placeholder renumbered, and that file is never swept into the renumbering commit; content already staged in the index leaves the placeholder unrenumbered rather than sweep the staged file into a \\u0060chore:\\u0060 commit that describes none of it.
